newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crude off amid Alaskan crude sales.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crude off amid Alaskan crude sales.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude oil prices fell Friday after two sales of Alaska crude, the region's benchmark, sold a sharply lower discounts, traders said.
Two cargoes of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude sold Thursday and Friday, at $2.10 and $2.07 a barrel under July West Texas Intermediate (WTI).
The previous ANS deal was done at $1.75 in late May.
Buyers and sellers were split on the current ANS market value, with refiners claiming $2.10 and producers $2.07.
The $2.10 deal was done between a Houston-based ANS producer and a U.S Northwest refiner, while the largest producer of ANS sold to a Hawaii refinery at $2.07.
A trader for the Hawaii refinery said the plant was forced to take the higher priced cargo because no other ANS sellers would delivery out to the Pacific Island.
But sellers said the refiner could have taken other Pacific crudes, such as Australian grades.
Outright prices for ANS were $16.80/16.93 a barrel, with discounts seen widening next week.

High volumes of imports, especially Ecuadorian and other South American grades, have undercut ANS prices in recent months, causing the discount to widen from 91 cents under in March to $1.75 in late May.
Heavier California grades remained unchanged this week.
